from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Vector Space Concept", 
                          ["Embeddings map words to coordinate points.", 
                           "Machines calculate distance between these vectors.", 
                           "Conceptually similar words are placed close together."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create grid and two icons representing "Cat" and "Dog"
        cat_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/machine.svg")
        dog_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/machine.svg")
        
        self.place_at_grid(cat_icon, 'C2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(dog_icon, 'D4', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        cat_label = Text("Cat", font_size=18, color=WHITE).next_to(cat_icon, UP, buff=0.1)
        dog_label = Text("Dog", font_size=18, color=WHITE).next_to(dog_icon, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cat_icon), FadeIn(dog_icon), FadeIn(cat_label), FadeIn(dog_label))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw a dashed line between the two points
        dist_line = DashedLine(cat_icon.get_center(), dog_icon.get_center(), color="#FF00FF")
        self.play(Create(dist_line))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Move the two points closer together
        new_cat_pos = self.grid['C3']
        new_dog_pos = self.grid['C4']
        
        self.play(
            cat_icon.animate.move_to(new_cat_pos),
            cat_label.animate.move_to(new_cat_pos + UP * 0.5),
            dog_icon.animate.move_to(new_dog_pos),
            dog_label.animate.move_to(new_dog_pos + UP * 0.5),
            UpdateFromFunc(dist_line, lambda m: m.put_start_and_end_on(cat_icon.get_center(), dog_icon.get_center()))
        )
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Scaling Up: From Transformer to LLM", 
                          ["Scaling stacks many Transformer layers together.", 
                           "Deep stacking captures subtle logic and nuance.", 
                           "LLMs represent vast networks of knowledge."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create multiple rectangular layers stacked vertically using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/server.svg]
        server_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/server.svg", color="#FFFFFF")
        
        layers = VGroup()
        for i in range(5):
            layer = server_icon.copy()
            # Fixed: Calculate row index by converting 'E' to index and subtracting i, then remapping to char
            row_char = chr(ord('E') - i)
            self.place_at_grid(layer, f"{row_char}3", scale_factor=0.5)
            layers.add(layer)
        
        self.play(Create(layers))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Pulse each layer to show depth and nuance being captured.
        pulses = VGroup()
        for layer in layers:
            pulse = layer.copy().set_color("#0000FF")
            pulses.add(pulse)
        
        self.play(Flash(layers, color="#0000FF", line_length=0.1, num_lines=10))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#0000FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Expand the stack to show the vast network of knowledge using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/network.svg]
        network_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/network.svg", color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_in_area(network_icon, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(layers, network_icon))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Training Loop: Predicting the Next Token", [
            "Training models predict the next token sequence.",
            "Models minimize prediction errors using backpropagation.",
            "Correct predictions reinforce internal weight adjustments.",
            "Continuous correction optimizes output accuracy.",
            "Iterative learning enables human-like language generation."
        ])
        
        # Assets
        computer = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/computer.svg")
        processor = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/processor.svg")
        
        # --- Animation for Line 1 ---
        # Show a sliding window over a token sequence using a computer.
        self.place_at_grid(computer, 'B2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(computer))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # --- Animation for Line 2 ---
        # Calculate the error between the prediction and the target.
        error_circle = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(error_circle, 'B5')
        self.play(Create(error_circle))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")
        
        # --- Animation for Line 3 ---
        # Show the backpropagation signal adjusting internal weights.
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid['B5'], end=self.grid['E5'], color="#00FFFF")
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # --- Animation for Line 4 ---
        # Update the weights to minimize the error.
        weight_rect = Rectangle(width=1, height=0.5, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(weight_rect, 'E2')
        self.play(Create(weight_rect))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # --- Animation for Line 5 ---
        # Show the model producing more accurate predictions iteratively on the processor.
        self.place_at_grid(processor, 'E5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(processor))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        self.wait(2)

        ])

outline.topic: Decoding Large Language Models and Transformers
outline.target_audience: University students with basic programming knowledge

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Vector Space Concept
sections.content: Introduce embeddings as coordinate points. Explain that machines don't understand words, but can calculate 'distance' between numerical vectors representing concepts.
sections.example: Represent 'Cat' and 'Dog' as points close together on a 2D graph, while 'Robot' is placed far away.

sections.title: The Transformer Core: Attention Mechanism
sections.content: Explain the 'Self-Attention' mechanism visually: instead of reading linearly, the model assigns weights (importance) to all words in a sentence simultaneously.
sections.example: In the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired', visualize lines connecting 'it' to 'animal' with thicker glow lines to show semantic focus.

sections.title: Scaling Up: From Transformer to LLM
sections.content: Discuss the 'Large' in LLM. Explain how stacking Transformer layers allows the model to capture complex relationships like syntax, nuance, and logic.
sections.example: A single Transformer block is like a library index card; an LLM is the entire library with thousands of cross-referenced shelves.

sections.title: The Training Loop: Predicting the Next Token
sections.content: Show the training process: the model receives a partial sequence and adjusts internal weights to minimize the error of the predicted next word.
sections.example: A 'Robot Teacher' providing an exam where the prompt is 'The sky is...' and the model gets 'blue' right; if it says 'green', it self-corrects via backpropagation.

sections.title: Real-world Application: Generative AI
sections.content: Synthesize how the previous concepts allow an LLM to generate creative content by sampling probabilities of the next probable tokens.
sections.example: Imagine a chatbot 'Chef-Bot' deciding between adding 'salt' or 'sugar' to a sentence about cooking, based on its training on millions of recipes.
